newsitem.title: UK: Brian Connolly, lead singer of Sweet, dies at 52.
newsitem.headline: Brian Connolly, lead singer of Sweet, dies at 52.

text.p: Brian Connolly, lead singer of the British 1970s "glam rock" band Sweet, died on Monday aged 52, a friend said.
Sweet had a clutch of Top 10 hits in the early 1970s, including the number one "Blockbuster".
Other hits included "Wig-Wam Bam", "Ballroom Blitz" and "Teenage Rampage" and the band sold about 50 million singles and albums in total.
Connolly, famous for his stack heels and long blond hair, died in hospital surrounded by friends and family after suffering renal failure after a heart attack, a friend said.

Once the band became famous, Connolly set about living the rock star life with zest, drinking vast quantities of alcohol at parties, often in the company of legendary party goer and Who drummer Keith Moon.
Touring in the United States gave him plenty of scope for wild living, Connolly once said. "They were wild, crazy days and nights, but booze was my downfall rather than drugs."
In 1981 he had two heart attacks. While in hospital recovering from the second, his heart stopped again at least six times.
